tagline: Up Big Stony Creek on an old railroad's trail.
intro: Near Pembroke, a New River town named in 1845 by a postmaster who came across the name in his reading, Big Stony Creek Road turns off and follows the creek up toward West Virginia. It keeps mostly to the line of the Big Stony Railway, which ran up the creek from the New River and was carried on by the Norfolk and Western to Potts Creek. The upper 34 miles of track were given up in 1934.
The road passes into Monroe County, West Virginia, and comes back into Virginia as Waiteville Road, which runs on to Route 311 at Paint Bank.

moments.title: Goldbond
moments.text: A Stony Creek settlement once called Kerns after a bread company, renamed for the Gold Bond wallboard of the National Gypsum works that came later.

moments.title: Paint Bank
moments.text: Between Potts and Peters mountains, the red clay of Potts Creek gave the Cherokee war paint and pottery, and later settlers paint and brick.
